- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and model overestimates prices, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot after spikes.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and model underestimates, slightly increase forecast to avoid prolonged underperformance.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model should not overreact to short-term spikes; dampen forecast momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model should not over-forecast beyond 10% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms bullish bias.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and model shows persistent over-forecasting, apply a 1–3% downward correction to align with historical mean reversion.  
- If model consistently under-forecasts during periods of high sentiment, adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven volatility.
